EQR-04.question_for_llm: Does the clause identify which breaches can justify relief (for example confidentiality or IP)?
EQR-04.why_it_matters: Named breaches limit use to cases where damages are not enough.

COI-01.question_for_llm: Does the clause require the parties to avoid conflicts of interest?
COI-01.met_when: The duty applies to both parties.
COI-01.partly_met_when: The duty applies to one party only.
COI-01.why_it_matters: A conflict can distort advice and decisions.

COI-02.question_for_llm: Does the clause describe what counts as a conflict of interest?
COI-02.why_it_matters: An undefined conflict cannot be tested.

COI-03.question_for_llm: Must a party disclose an actual or possible conflict?
COI-03.met_when: A duty is stated with a definite timeframe.
COI-03.partly_met_when: A duty is stated without a timeframe.
COI-03.why_it_matters: A conflict that is not disclosed cannot be managed.

COI-04.question_for_llm: Does the clause say what follows if a conflict arises (for example stop the activity or terminate)?
COI-04.met_when: A consequence is stated with how it works.
COI-04.partly_met_when: A consequence is mentioned without how it works.
COI-04.why_it_matters: A duty with no consequence has no practical effect.

SUR-01.question_for_llm: Does the clause list the provisions that continue after expiry or termination?
SUR-01.met_when: Specific provisions or sections are listed.
SUR-01.partly_met_when: General wording is used (for example 'provisions that by their nature survive').
SUR-01.why_it_matters: Key protections such as confidentiality and liability must continue after exit.

SUR-02.question_for_llm: Does the clause keep rights and liabilities that arose before termination?
SUR-02.why_it_matters: Termination should not erase debts or claims already incurred.

SUR-03.applies_when: The clause says some provisions continue
SUR-03.question_for_llm: Is the period for which they continue stated?
SUR-03.met_when: A definite period or 'indefinitely' is stated for each provision or overall.
SUR-03.why_it_matters: An unstated period leaves duties open to argument.

SUR-04.question_for_llm: Does survival protect both parties' interests?
SUR-04.not_met_when: Only one party's protections survive and the other's end.
SUR-04.why_it_matters: One-way survival lets one party walk away from its duties.

CTP-01.question_for_llm: Does the clause allow the agreement to be signed in separate counterparts?
CTP-01.why_it_matters: It lets parties sign separately without questioning validity.

CTP-02.question_for_llm: Does the clause say the counterparts together form one agreement?
CTP-02.why_it_matters: It avoids separate signed copies being treated as separate contracts.

CTP-03.question_for_llm: Does the clause allow electronic signature and electronic delivery of signed copies?
CTP-03.why_it_matters: It confirms that remote signing is valid.

CTP-04.question_for_llm: Does the clause say when the agreement takes effect if counterparts are signed on different dates?
CTP-04.why_it_matters: It fixes the date from which obligations run.

TOE-01.question_for_llm: Does the clause identify which obligations or dates time is of the essence for?
TOE-01.met_when: Specific obligations or dates are named.
TOE-01.partly_met_when: It applies to all obligations in general terms.
TOE-01.not_met_when: No obligation or date is identified.
TOE-01.why_it_matters: Making every date strict can turn a small delay into a breach.

TOE-02.question_for_llm: Does the clause apply to both parties' obligations?
TOE-02.partly_met_when: It applies to one party only.
TOE-02.not_met_when: It does not say whose obligations it covers.
TOE-02.why_it_matters: Strict timing for one party only is one-sided.

TOE-03.question_for_llm: Does the clause say what follows if the time is missed?
TOE-03.met_when: A consequence is stated with how it works.
TOE-03.partly_met_when: A consequence is mentioned without how it works.
TOE-03.why_it_matters: A time limit with no consequence has no practical effect.

TOE-04.criterion: Extension for causes outside a party's control
TOE-04.question_for_llm: Does the clause allow more time where delay is caused by the other party or an excused event?
TOE-04.met_when: Extension is allowed and the causes are named.
TOE-04.partly_met_when: Extension is allowed in general terms.
TOE-04.why_it_matters: A strict date should not run against a party prevented from meeting it.

TAX-01.question_for_llm: Does the clause say which party bears each tax it covers (for example sales or transaction tax and withholding)?
TAX-01.met_when: The responsible party is stated for each tax covered.
TAX-01.partly_met_when: It is stated for some only.
TAX-01.why_it_matters: Unexpected tax changes the real cost of the deal.

TAX-02.question_for_llm: Does the clause state whether fees include taxes?
TAX-02.why_it_matters: The price is uncertain until this is clear.

TAX-03.applies_when: The clause deals with withholding tax or gross-up
TAX-03.question_for_llm: Are the treatment of withholding and the documents needed stated?
TAX-03.met_when: Both the treatment and the documents are stated.
TAX-03.why_it_matters: Withholding can reduce what a party actually receives.

TAX-04.question_for_llm: Must the parties provide tax invoices, exemption certificates or other documents?
TAX-04.why_it_matters: Missing documents can block tax relief.

TAX-05.question_for_llm: Does the clause say each party bears taxes on its own income and personnel?
TAX-05.why_it_matters: It keeps a party from being billed for the other's tax.

MSC-01.question_for_llm: Does each right or duty the clause creates say who, what and when?
MSC-01.met_when: Each states who, what and when.
MSC-01.why_it_matters: A vague right or duty cannot be applied.

MSC-02.question_for_llm: Does the clause avoid terms that belong in a specific clause type (for example liability, payment or termination)?
MSC-02.partly_met_when: Minor terms of another type are present.
MSC-02.not_met_when: Terms of another type are present.
MSC-02.why_it_matters: Terms hidden in a catch-all clause are easy to miss in review.

MSC-03.question_for_llm: Do the rights in the clause apply to both parties in the same way?
MSC-03.why_it_matters: A one-sided term in a catch-all clause is easily overlooked.

MSC-04.question_for_llm: Does any duty in the clause have a consequence or a way to act on it if it is not followed?
MSC-04.met_when: A consequence or route is stated.
MSC-04.partly_met_when: It is mentioned without how it works.
MSC-04.why_it_matters: A duty with no consequence gives no practical way to act.

MSC-05.applies_when: The clause says it applies despite other terms
MSC-05.question_for_llm: Does the clause name the terms it overrides?
MSC-05.partly_met_when: Some are named and some are general.
MSC-05.not_met_when: The override is general ('notwithstanding anything else').
MSC-05.why_it_matters: A general override can undo protections elsewhere.

MSC-06.applies_when: The clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements
MSC-06.question_for_llm: Does each party appoint a named person or role to manage the relationship?
MSC-06.met_when: Both parties appoint a person or role.
MSC-06.why_it_matters: Without a named contact, issues have no clear owner.

MSC-07.applies_when: The clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements
MSC-07.question_for_llm: Does the clause say how often governance meetings or reviews take place?
MSC-07.partly_met_when: Only vague wording is used (for example 'regularly', 'as needed').
MSC-07.why_it_matters: Without a set rhythm, reviews tend not to happen.

MSC-08.applies_when: The clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements
MSC-08.question_for_llm: Does the clause require progress or performance reports, with their content or frequency stated?
MSC-08.met_when: Reports are required and both content and frequency are stated.
MSC-08.partly_met_when: Reports are required but only one of content or frequency is stated.
MSC-08.why_it_matters: Without reports, performance cannot be checked.

MSC-09.applies_when: The clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements
MSC-09.question_for_llm: Does the clause set how unresolved issues are escalated (levels or steps)?
MSC-09.met_when: Levels or steps are stated, with who is involved.
MSC-09.why_it_matters: A defined route settles issues before they become disputes.

MSC-10.applies_when: The clause sets up governance, review or relationship-management arrangements
MSC-10.question_for_llm: Does the clause say what the representatives can decide, and that their decisions do not change the agreement unless formally agreed?
MSC-10.why_it_matters: Informal decisions can be argued to have changed the contract.

PTY-01.question_for_llm: Is the full legal name of each party stated?
PTY-01.met_when: The full legal name of every party is stated.
PTY-01.partly_met_when: Some names are incomplete or abbreviated.
PTY-01.why_it_matters: A wrong or incomplete name can make the agreement unenforceable against the real entity.

PTY-02.question_for_llm: For each party, are the entity type and registration details (for example jurisdiction of incorporation and registration number) stated?
PTY-02.met_when: Both are stated for every party.
PTY-02.partly_met_when: They are stated for some parties or only partly.
PTY-02.why_it_matters: They allow the entity to be verified.

PTY-03.question_for_llm: Is an address stated for each party?
PTY-03.met_when: An address is stated for every party.
PTY-03.partly_met_when: An address is stated for some parties.

PTY-04.question_for_llm: Is each party given a defined short name or role (for example 'Customer', 'Supplier') used consistently?
PTY-04.met_when: Labels are defined and used consistently.
PTY-04.partly_met_when: Labels are defined but used inconsistently.
PTY-04.why_it_matters: Inconsistent labels create doubt about who owes what.

PTY-05.question_for_llm: Are the party names written consistently within the block (spelling and form)?
PTY-05.why_it_matters: Inconsistent names suggest drafting errors or the wrong entity.

PTY-06.applies_when: The document is a final or executed version
PTY-06.question_for_llm: Are all fields filled in, with no blanks or bracketed placeholders?
PTY-06.why_it_matters: A blank where a party detail belongs leaves the agreement incomplete.

PRM-01.question_for_llm: Does the preamble state the agreement's date or effective date?
PRM-01.met_when: A definite date, or a definite way to work it out, is stated.
PRM-01.partly_met_when: A date is referred to but left blank or unclear.
PRM-01.why_it_matters: Time periods in the agreement often run from this date.

PRM-02.question_for_llm: Are the parties referred to in the same way as they are named or labelled in the preamble?
PRM-02.why_it_matters: Inconsistent references create doubt about who is bound.

PRM-03.question_for_llm: Does the preamble identify the agreement by title or type?
PRM-03.met_when: A title or type is stated.
PRM-03.why_it_matters: It identifies what document is being agreed.

PRM-04.applies_when: The document is a final or executed version
PRM-04.question_for_llm: Are all fields filled in, with no blanks or bracketed placeholders?
PRM-04.why_it_matters: Leftover blanks suggest an unfinished document.

PRM-05.question_for_llm: Does the preamble avoid creating obligations or rights?
PRM-05.met_when: It only identifies the agreement and its parties.
PRM-05.not_met_when: It contains an obligation or right.
PRM-05.why_it_matters: Obligations placed in a preamble are easy to miss and may not be enforceable.

REC-01.question_for_llm: Do the recitals avoid creating obligations or rights?
REC-01.not_met_when: A recital contains an obligation or right.
REC-01.why_it_matters: Obligations placed in recitals may not be enforceable and are easy to miss.

REC-02.question_for_llm: Do the recitals state the background (who the parties are and why they are contracting)?
REC-02.met_when: The background states why the agreement is made.
REC-02.partly_met_when: The background is stated in general terms.
REC-02.why_it_matters: Clear background helps explain intent if terms are unclear.

REC-03.question_for_llm: Are the parties referred to by the same names or labels throughout the recitals?
REC-03.met_when: The same names or labels are used.
REC-03.why_it_matters: Inconsistent names raise doubt about who is meant.

REC-04.applies_when: The document is a final or executed version
REC-04.question_for_llm: Are the recitals free of unfilled placeholders (for example [date], [party])?
REC-04.why_it_matters: A placeholder in a final copy shows the document is not finished.

TOC-01.question_for_llm: Do the listed entries match the headings in the document?
TOC-01.partly_met_when: A few entries do not match.
TOC-01.why_it_matters: Mismatches can mean the document changed after the contents were built.

TOC-02.question_for_llm: Is every main heading and schedule in the document listed?

TOC-03.question_for_llm: Are the page or clause references correct?
TOC-03.why_it_matters: Wrong references make the document harder to use.

SIG-01.applies_when: The document is an execution copy or includes a signature block section
SIG-01.question_for_llm: Is there a signature block for every party intended to execute the agreement?
SIG-01.met_when: A signature block is provided for each party, or the document is clearly an in-progress draft/excerpt.
SIG-01.not_met_when: A formal execution block is present but omits one of the named contracting parties.
SIG-01.why_it_matters: A party that does not sign may not be bound.

SIG-02.question_for_llm: Is the signatory's name and title stated or provided for each party?
SIG-02.met_when: Name and title are given for every party.
SIG-02.partly_met_when: Only one of name or title is given, or it is given for some parties.
SIG-02.why_it_matters: It shows who signed and whether they had authority.

SIG-03.question_for_llm: Is there a date, or a date line, for each party's signature?
SIG-03.met_when: A date or date line is given for every party.
SIG-03.partly_met_when: It is given for some parties.
SIG-03.why_it_matters: It fixes when each party agreed.

SIG-04.question_for_llm: Does the block state the capacity in which each person signs (for example director, authorised signatory)?
SIG-04.met_when: Capacity is stated for every signatory.
SIG-04.partly_met_when: It is stated for some signatories.
SIG-04.why_it_matters: It reduces the risk that the signatory lacked authority.

SIG-05.applies_when: The document is an executed version
SIG-05.question_for_llm: Is a signature present for every party?
SIG-05.why_it_matters: An unsigned executed copy is not evidence of agreement.

SCH-01.question_for_llm: Does the schedule or exhibit carry a unique number or letter?
SCH-01.met_when: A unique number or letter is shown.
SCH-01.not_met_when: No number or letter is shown.
SCH-01.why_it_matters: References in the agreement cannot find an unnumbered schedule.

SCH-02.question_for_llm: Does the schedule or exhibit have a title that states its subject?
SCH-02.partly_met_when: A generic title is used (for example 'Annex').
SCH-02.why_it_matters: A clear title lets reviewers find the right terms.

SCH-03.question_for_llm: Does the schedule or exhibit say which agreement or clause it belongs to?
SCH-03.met_when: The agreement and clause are named.
SCH-03.partly_met_when: The agreement is named without a clause.
SCH-03.why_it_matters: An unlinked schedule may not be part of the contract.

SCH-04.applies_when: The document refers to schedules or exhibits elsewhere
SCH-04.question_for_llm: Compared with how the rest of the document refers to it, does the schedule's number and title match?
SCH-04.why_it_matters: A mismatch means a reference points to the wrong or no schedule.

SCH-05.applies_when: The document is a final or executed version
SCH-05.question_for_llm: Is the schedule or exhibit free of unfilled placeholders?
SCH-05.why_it_matters: A placeholder in a final copy shows the document is not finished.

PGF-01.question_for_llm: Does the content consist only of headers, footers, page numbers, watermarks or document marks?
PGF-01.partly_met_when: It is mixed with some body text.
PGF-01.why_it_matters: Substantive text here usually means a clause was misclassified.

PGF-02.question_for_llm: Does the content avoid operative language (obligations, rights, restrictions, payment or liability wording)?
PGF-02.partly_met_when: Some wording could be read as operative.
PGF-02.why_it_matters: Operative text here is likely to be missed in review.

PGF-03.criterion: No clause text broken by a page
PGF-03.question_for_llm: Is the content free of clause text split off by a page break?
PGF-03.met_when: No clause text is split off.
PGF-03.partly_met_when: A fragment of a sentence is present.
PGF-03.not_met_when: A clause or part of a clause is present.
PGF-03.why_it_matters: Split text can hide part of a clause from its review.

NTR-01.question_for_llm: Does the content avoid operative language (obligations, rights, restrictions, payment or liability wording)?
NTR-01.partly_met_when: Some wording could be read as operative.
NTR-01.why_it_matters: A note that contains an obligation may be missed or may not bind.

NTR-02.question_for_llm: Does each note or reference identify the item it points to (clause, document or source)?
NTR-02.why_it_matters: A reference that points nowhere cannot be checked.

NTR-03.criterion: Clearly a note, not a clause
NTR-03.question_for_llm: Is the content identifiable as a note, footnote or reference rather than a clause?
NTR-03.met_when: It is clearly identifiable as a note or reference.
NTR-03.not_met_when: It cannot be told apart from a clause.
NTR-03.why_it_matters: Mistaking a note for a clause (or the reverse) changes what is binding.

NTR-04.question_for_llm: Is the content free of drafting comments, tracked-change marks or notes to draft?
NTR-04.why_it_matters: Drafting notes left in a final copy can show unfinished or disputed terms.

ONC-01.question_for_llm: Does the content avoid operative language (obligations, rights, restrictions, payment or liability wording)?
ONC-01.partly_met_when: Some wording could be read as operative.
ONC-01.why_it_matters: Operative text here usually means a clause was misclassified.

ONC-02.question_for_llm: Is the content free of drafting artefacts (placeholders, bracketed text, comments, drafting notes)?

ONC-03.question_for_llm: Does the content have a heading or label that says what it is?
ONC-03.met_when: A heading or label is present.
ONC-03.why_it_matters: Unlabelled content is hard to place within the agreement.
